Task 6.0: Lab Prototype Testing and Analysis (M-2.6.1, GNG-2A, GNG-2B, GNG-2C) Lab Prototype Experimental Setup Page 41 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. Element 16’s lab prototype sulfur TES unit consists of an outer vessel that holds 5 tons of sulfur and three internal serpentine tube circuits connected in parallel that circulate the thermal oil heat transfer fluid (HTF) as shown In Figure 20. The sulfur TES was equipped with approximately 80 thermocouples on the exterior surface of the tank, installed at various circumferential positions at 5 different axial locations – z = ± 24”, ± 48”, 0” (Figure 20). The z-axis position was measured from the center of the tank. The spatial tank surface temperature distribution measured by the external thermocouples during cyclic charge/discharge operation mode were used to calculate the thermal stresses and ensure the criteria (GNG-2C) for mechanical factor of safety was satisfied. The sulfur TES was equipped with 31 internal thermocouples, 11 of which were installed through the front flanges and the rest installed through the top flanges at the time of commissioning (Figure 21). The internal thermocouples allowed for monitoring of spatial and transient temperature distribution within molten sulfur during charge, discharge, and dormant modes and to calculate the heat transfer rate and energy stored within sulfur. In addition, these temperature measurements were used to validate the computational tools developed in Task 7. Other sensors include pressure gauge and gas monitoring instruments, all of which were connected to a data acquisition system (DAQ) for data collection and storage. The data from the sensors were recorded at three-minute intervals. Figures 22 and 23 show the HTF electric heater integrated with the sulfur TES lab prototype, the heater control panels and water metering pump along with water tank connected to the tube-in-tube discharge heat exchanger (heat sink) that was controlled to maintain desired HTF inlet temperature into the TES during discharge operation. The operation of the HTF electric heater and HTF pump was independently controlled by a PID controller and voltage/current signal generator, respectively.
